question: The range of the real valued function $f(x)=\sqrt{\;\frac{x^{2}+2 x+8}{x^{2}+2 x+4}}$ is

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: 👈: Video Solution $f(x)=\sqrt{\;\frac{x^2+2 x+8}{x^2+2 x+4}}$ Let $y=\;\frac{x^2+2 x+8}{x^2+2 x+4}$ $[ \because f(x)=\sqrt{y}]$ $\;\Rightarrow \;\; y x^2+2 x y+4 y=x^2+2 x+8$ $\;\Rightarrow \;\; (y-1) x^2+2 x(y-1)+4 y-8=0$ For $x$ to be real, discriminant of equation must be greater than equals to zero. $\;\{ [2(y-1)]^2-4(y-1)(4 y-8) \} \ge 0$ $\Rightarrow 4(y-1)^2-4(y-1) 4(y-2) \ge 0$ $\Rightarrow\;(y-1)^2-(y-1) 4(y-2) \ge 0$ $\Rightarrow\;(y-1)[y-1-4 y+8] \ge 0$ $\Rightarrow\;(y-1)(-3 y+7) \ge 0$ $\Rightarrow\;y\;=1,\;\frac{7}{3}$ $\therefore \;\; (y-1)(-3 y+7) \ge 0 \Rightarrow y \in (1,\;\frac{7}{3}]$ $[ \because .$ At $y=1, x^2+2 x+4 \neq x^2+2 x+8]$ $\; \because \;\; y \in (1,\;\frac{7}{3}]$ $\therefore\; f(x) \in (1, \sqrt{\;\frac{7}{3}}] .$ © examsnet.com

question: If $f(x)=\sqrt{2-x^{2}}$ and $g(x)=\log(1-x)$ are two real valued functions then the domain of the function $(f+g)(x)$ is

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: 👈: Video Solution $f(x)=\sqrt{2-x^2}$ and $g(x)=\log(1-x)$ $(f+g)(x)=f(x)+g(x)$ $=\sqrt{2-x^2}+\log(1-x)$ $2-x^2 \geq 0$ $\Rightarrow x^2 \leq 2$ $\Rightarrow |x| \leq \sqrt{2}$ $\Rightarrow -\sqrt{2} \leq x \leq \sqrt{2}$ Also, $1-x>0 \Rightarrow x<1$ Required domain : $-\sqrt{2} \leq x \leq \sqrt{2} \cap x<1$ $\Rightarrow -\sqrt{2} \leq x < 1$ © examsnet.com

question: For $i=1,2,3$ and $j=1,2,3$ If $a_{i}^{2}+b_{i}^{2}+c_{i}^{2}=1, a_{i}a_{j}+b_{i}b_{j}+c_{i}c_{j}=0, \; \; \forall i \neq j$ and $A=\begin{bmatrix} a_1 & a_2 & a_3 \\ b_1 & b_2 & b_3 \\ c_1 & c_2 & c_3 \end{bmatrix}$ then $\det(AA^{T})=$

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: 👈: Video Solution Given, $a_i^2+b_1^2+c_i^2\;=1$ $a_1^2+b_1^2+c_1^2\;=1$ $a_2^2+b_2^2+c_2^2\;=1$ $a_3^2+b_3^2+c_3^2\;=1$ Given, $a_i a_j+b_i b_j+c_j c_j=0$ $[i, j=1,2,3, i \neq j]$ Let $\text{bo}\,p\;=a_1\text{bo}\,i+b_1\text{bo}\,j+c_1\text{bo}\,k$ $\text{bo}\,q\;=a_2\text{bo}\,i+b_2\text{bo}\,j+c_2\text{bo}\,k$ $\text{bo}\,r\;=a_3\text{bo}\,i+b_3\text{bo}\,j+c_3\text{bo}\,k$ $|\text{bo}\,p|\;=|\text{bo}\,q|=|\text{bo}\,r|=1$ $\text{bo}\,p \cdot \text{bo}\,q\;= (a_1\text{bo}\,i+b_1\text{bo}\,j+c_1\text{bo}\,k) \cdot (a_2\text{bo}\,i+b_2\text{bo}\,j+c_3\text{bo}\,k)$ $\;=a_1 a_2+b_1 b_2+c_1 c_2=0$ $\Rightarrow \text{bo}\,p \perp \text{bo}\,q$ Similarly, $\text{bo}\,q \perp \text{bo}\,r, \text{bo}\,r \perp \text{bo}\,p$ Now, $A=\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & a_2 & a_3 \\ b_1 & b_2 & b_3 \\ c_1 & c_2 & c_3 \end{vmatrix}=\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} \text{bo}\,p & \text{bo}\,q & \text{bo}\,r \end{bmatrix}=1$ $\;\Rightarrow \det(A A^{T}) =1$ © examsnet.com

question: If $A = \; \frac{1}{7} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 & 6 \\ -6 & -3 & 2 \\ -2 & 6 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ , then

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: 👈: Video Solution $A = \; \frac{1}{7} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 & 6 \\ -6 & -3 & 2 \\ -2 & 6 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ $|A| = \; \frac{1}{7^3} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 & 6 \\ -6 & -3 & 2 \\ -2 & 6 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ $[\because \det(k A) = k^n \det A]$ $= \frac{1}{7^3} \left[ 3(-9-12) + 2(-18+4) + 6(-36-6) \right]$ $= \frac{1}{7^3} \left[ -63 -28 -252 \right]$ $= \frac{-343}{7^3} = -1 \neq 0$ $\operatorname{Adj}(A) = \frac{1}{7^2} \begin{bmatrix} -21 & 14 & -42 \\ 42 & 21 & -14 \\ 14 & -42 & -21 \end{bmatrix}^\tau$ $[\because \operatorname{adj}(k A) = k^{n-1} \operatorname{adj} A]$ $= \frac{1}{7^2} \begin{bmatrix} -21 & 42 & 14 \\ 14 & 21 & -42 \\ -42 & -14 & -21 \end{bmatrix}$ Now, $A^{-1} = \frac{\operatorname{adj}(A)}{|A|} = \frac{-1}{7^2} \begin{bmatrix} -21 & 42 & 14 \\ 14 & 21 & -42 \\ -42 & -14 & -21 \end{bmatrix}$ $= \frac{1}{7} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -6 & -2 \\ -2 & -3 & 6 \\ 6 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ $A^{-1} = A^T$ © examsnet.com

question: If the identity $\cos^{4} \theta = a \cos 4\theta + b \cos 2\theta + c$ holds for some $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q}$ , then $(a, b, c) =$

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: 👈: Video Solution $\cos^{4} \theta = a \cdot \cos 4\theta + b \cos 2\theta + c$ $\; \Rightarrow \;\; \cos^{4} \theta = a [2 \cos^{2} 2\theta - 1] + b [2 \cos^{2} \theta - 1] + c$ $\; \Rightarrow \;\; \cos^{4} \theta = a \cdot 2 \cos^{2} 2\theta - a + 2 b \cos^{2} \theta - b + c$ $\; \Rightarrow \;\; \cos^{4} \theta = 2 a (\cos 2\theta)^2 + 2 b \cos^{2} \theta - a - b + c$ $\; \Rightarrow \;\; \cos^{4} \theta = 2 a (2 \cos^{2} \theta - 1)^2 + 2 b \cos^{2} \theta - a - b + c$ $\; \Rightarrow \;\; \cos^{4} \theta = 2 a (4 \cos^{4} \theta + 1 - 4 \cos^{2} \theta) + 2 b \cos^{2} \theta - a - b + c$ $\Rightarrow \cos^{4} \theta = 8 a \cos^{4} \theta \; + 2 a - 8 a \cos^{2} \theta \; + 2 b \cos^{2} \theta - a - b + c$ $\Rightarrow \cos^{4} \theta = 8 a \cos^{4} \theta + \cos^{2} \theta (-8 a + 2 b) + a - b + c$ On comparing the corresponding coefficients, we get $8 a = 1, -8 a + 2 b = 0$ and $a - b + c = 0$ $\Rightarrow \;\; a = \frac{1}{8}$ $\therefore \; -8 \left(\frac{1}{8}\right) + 2 b = 0$ gives $b = \frac{1}{2}$ $\; \text{ and } \;\; \frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{2} + c = 0$ gives $c = \frac{3}{8}$ © examsnet.com

Using Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, $\Delta x \cdot m \Delta v = \frac{h}{4 \pi}$ As $\Delta x = \Delta v,$ So, $\Delta v \cdot m \Delta v = \frac{h}{4 \pi}$ On multiplying both sides with $m$ , we get $m \Delta v \cdot m \Delta v = \frac{m h}{4 \pi}$ Thus, $\;\;  \Delta p^2 = \frac{m h}{4 \pi} \Rightarrow \Delta p = \sqrt{\frac{m h}{4 \pi}}$ . Hence, $\;\;  \Delta p = \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{m h}{\pi}}$ © examsnet.com

question: A solid sphere of radius $R$ has its outer half removed, so that its radius becomes $\left(\frac{R}{2}\right)$ . Then its moment of inertia about the diameter is

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: (a) $\mathrm{P}_4$ reacts with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ . On heating, it gives $\mathrm{NaH}_2\mathrm{PO}_2$ and $\mathrm{PH}_3$ . $\mathrm{P}_4 + 3\mathrm{NaOH} + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 3\mathrm{NaH}_2\mathrm{PO}_2 + \mathrm{PH}_3$ This reaction is a disproportionation reaction as oxidation state of $\mathrm{P}$ changes from 0 to +1 and -3 . Which implies that, it undergoes oxidation and reduction simultaneously. $\mathrm{S}_8$ reacts with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ on heating to given $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}$ and $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ . $\mathrm{S}_8 + 12\mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S} + 2\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ This reaction is a disproportionation reaction as oxidation state of $\mathrm{S}$ changes from 0 to -2 and +2 . Which implies that, it undergoes oxidation and reduction simultaneously. But, $\mathrm{N}_2$ is an inert gas. So, it does not react with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ . Thus, only $\mathrm{P}_4$ and $\mathrm{S}_8$ undergo disproportionation when heated with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution. © examsnet.com

subject: Chemistry
question: Identify the correct statements about the anomalous behavior of Boron I. Boron trihalides can form dimeric structures. II. Boron shows $+1$ as stable oxidation state III. Maximum covalency of Boron is four. IV. Boron does not form $\mathrm{BF}_{6}^{6-}$ ion.

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: (I) Size of boron atom is very small, so it cannot accomodate 4 large halide atoms and thus, does not form dimer. Also, the electron deficiency of boron is removed by $p\pi-p\pi$ back-bonding. Hence, the boron trihalides do not form dimers. (II) In boron family, as we move down the group, two oxidation states are shown by them, i.e. +1 and +3 . However, boron shows only +3 oxidation state because of the absence of inert pair effect. Boron does not show +1 oxidation state. (III) Boron shows a maximum covalency of four because of absent of $d$ -orbitals. (IV) Boron does not form $\mathrm{BF}_6^{6-}$ ion because of absence of empty $d$ -orbitals. Hence, only statements III and IV are correct. © examsnet.com
